title: Well-foundedness of an ordinal carries over to its natural product with any finite coefficient
source_title: Conservation of Ramsey's theorem for pairs and well-foundedness

standard_prerequisites.name: Natural sum and natural product of ordinals below epsilon_0
standard_prerequisites.statement: For ordinals alpha and beta below epsilon_0 written with a common family of exponents, the natural sum is obtained by adding the coefficients of like powers of omega, and alpha ntimes k is the natural sum of alpha with itself k times; the article's own definition is retained at source lines 392-398, together with the comparison alpha ntimes k at most alpha times omega at source line 400.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma concludes WF(alpha ntimes k) from WF(alpha), so both the natural product and its comparison with the usual product must be available.

standard_prerequisites.name: Theories RCA_0 and the well-foundedness statement WF
standard_prerequisites.statement: RCA_0 is the standard base theory of reverse mathematics, and WF(alpha) states that the ordinal alpha is well founded; a model M satisfies WF(alpha) when it has no M-infinite descending sequence of ordinals below alpha; the article uses these notations throughout, for instance when it defines the Pi^1_1 proof-theoretic ordinal in its introduction.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is stated for a model M of RCA_0 plus WF(alpha) and concludes WF(alpha ntimes k) inside the same model.

core_obligations: Read the hypothesis: M = (M,S) is a model of RCA_0 plus WF(alpha) for an ordinal alpha below epsilon_0 (source line 412).

Use the comparison of the natural product with the usual ordinal product: for every k in M one has alpha ntimes k at most alpha times omega (source line 416 and the retained context at source line 400).
Invoke the fact, provable in RCA_0, that the product of two well-orders is a well-order, that is RCA_0 proves WF(alpha) implies WF(alpha times omega) (source line 416).

Combine the dominance with the implication to transfer well-foundedness downwards: since alpha ntimes k embeds into alpha times omega, no M-infinite descending sequence below alpha ntimes k exists inside M, whence M satisfies WF(alpha ntimes k) for every k in M (source lines 412 and 416).

proof_roadmap.step: Fix the model M, the ordinal alpha below epsilon_0 and its well-foundedness.
Recall that alpha ntimes k is at most alpha times omega for every k.
Use that RCA_0 proves WF(alpha) implies WF(alpha times omega) because products of well-orders are well-orders.
Conclude the desired well-foundedness of the natural product.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2402.11616v3 的 Lemma lem:wf-product（源 411-413 行，证明 415-423 行）：若 M 是 RCA_0 加 WF(alpha)（alpha < epsilon_0）的模型，则对每个 k 属于 M，M 也满足 WF(alpha ⨯ k)，其中 ⨯ 是自然积。证明的关键不是例行核验：必须把「自然积」与「通常的序数积」这两个不同的运算分开，先用作者在 400 行记下的比较 alpha ⨯ k <= alpha × omega（对每个 k 成立），再调用 RCA_0 可证的「良序之积是良序」即 RCA_0 ⊢ WF(alpha) -> WF(alpha × omega)（416 行），最后由「子序数良序」把良基性传递回自然积；三步中任一步用错运算（自然积 vs 通常积）都会得到错误的界。难点在于两个积运算的区分与传递方向；原文位置在证明的 416 行与保留语境 400 行。
